title: US Lead in AI Over China Narrows After DeepSeek Gains, BI Says
source_used: The Edge Malaysia, carrying Bloomberg text
key_facts: Bloomberg Intelligence (BI) senior analyst Robert Lea wrote in a report on Monday (5 Oct 2026) that the US lead in AI over China has narrowed to a record low
Top Chinese models lag US rivals by about 3% on benchmark scores, down from about 9% in May and 15% earlier in the year
The narrowing follows the September release of DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash
V4.1 Flash ranked sixth on LiveBench last month; DeepSeek scored 81.1 against Anthropic's best 83.4
Only three of the top 15 LiveBench models are Chinese
Lea cautioned that rankings shift and Chinese models face US scrutiny and possible bans over distillation allegations
He said the Chinese AI industry could stay unprofitable until 2030, with more than 1,100 large language models in a price war
quote_evidence: Top Chinese models lag their US rivals by just 3% on benchmark scores after the September release of DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash, BI senior analyst Robert Lea wrote in a report Monday.
The Asian country's progress "casts further doubt on the long-term sustainability of US technological supremacy in AI," Lea said.
why_it_matters_hint: Gains by Chinese models raise questions about the value of US chip export limits.
notes: Bloomberg blocked (403). Read The Edge Malaysia, which carries the Bloomberg text; Bloomberg is the source. Analyst opinion based on one benchmark (LiveBench).
